quandoUsar: Single choice among text options where the rotating gesture is part of the experience: camera lens, mode, period.
Touch screens or ones with a mouse wheel, where dragging along the arc or scrolling is more direct than opening a menu.
Ordered sets where seeing the current option and its neighbors is enough: labels fade with distance and disappear a little over three positions from the apex.
quandoEvitar: Use `segmented-control` when there are few options and all need to be visible at the same time.
Use `wheel-picker` for vertical reels of time or date, with several columns.
Use `select` in dense forms: the horizontal arc takes 30rem by 8rem by default.

teclado.acao: Rotates to the next enabled option.
Rotates to the previous enabled option.
Goes to the first or last enabled option.

acessibilidade: The root is a focusable `role="listbox"` with `aria-activedescendant` pointing to the chosen option; each label is a `role="option"` with `aria-selected`.
`label` is required and becomes the `aria-label`; `aria-orientation` becomes `vertical` on the `left` and `right` arcs.
Options with `disabled` appear struck through, get `aria-disabled`, and the disc never stops on them, whether by key, wheel, click, or drag.
movimento: The disc rotates to the option with a gentle spring and, on releasing a drag, inherits the gesture's velocity before settling on the nearest enabled option.
The apex brackets adjust with a spring to the width of the nearest label, and labels shrink and fade as they move away.
Beyond the ends the drag offers elastic resistance; with “reduce motion” on, disc and brackets jump straight to the final position.
responsivo: The `top` or `bottom` arc measures 30rem by 8rem (variables `--span` and `--depth`, adjustable via `style`) and respects `max-width: 100%`; the ends fade out through a mask.
On touch, the horizontal arc lets the page scroll vertically (`touch-action: pan-y`) and the side arcs, horizontally.
desempenho: Label widths are measured in layout and again when fonts load, and each option tracks the disc position on every frame: keep the list short.
notasIA: `options` is `{ value, label?, disabled? }[]` with a unique `value`, and the component's `label` is required; use `value` + `onValueChange` or `defaultValue` (without it, the first enabled option applies).
`side` chooses the disc face (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`), a larger `radius` makes the arc flatter, and `gap` fixes the distance between options, which by default follows each label's width.
Over the component, the mouse wheel rotates the disc instead of scrolling the page (scrolling only returns at the ends): do not put it in the way of a long scroll.
